outcomes.original: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning (Planning Code Section 303). What to say: Submit the CUA application online through SF Planning's portal, including the project description, floor plans showing the bar area and occupant load, a operations plan describing hours (if closing before midnight state that clearly), patron management, and any soundproofing or odor control measures. Pay the CUA application fee (approximately $3,100 for a no-construction CUA as of 2026–27, higher if construction cost exceeds thresholds; confirm the current fee schedule). The application triggers a 300-foot mailed notice to property owners, a posted notice at the site for 30 days, and assignment to a planner for environmental review (likely a categorical exemption for an existing commercial space) and a hearing date. Schedule a pre-application meeting with the assigned planner to review the operations plan and any neighborhood concerns before the hearing. The hearing will be before the P…

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain Planning Commission approval of the CUA at the public hearing. What to say: At the Commission hearing, present the operations plan and respond to any public comment. Emphasize the business's fit with the neighborhood (Chinatown visitor and arts corridor), the existing retail use at the address, measures to manage noise and litter (community liaison, posted exit notices, daily sidewalk monitoring), and compliance with the conditions imposed at 690 Sacramento Street (same district, 2023). If the Commission approves the CUA, a 30-day appeal period follows (Planning Code Section 308.1); if no appeal is filed or an appeal is denied, the CUA becomes effective and you may proceed to the building permit and ABC application. If the Commission continues the hearing for revisions, address the requested changes and return for approval.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements and change of use, after the CUA is effective. What to say: Submit the building permit application with architectural plans stamped by a licensed architect, showing the bar layout, sinks, restrooms, ADA compliance, finishes, mechanical systems, and the occupant load calculation. The application will be routed to Planning for zoning conformance (Planning Code Section 175); Planning will confirm that CUA 2023-005339CUA (or your case number) has been approved and issue a zoning referral approval. DBI will also route the permit to other departments (Fire, DPH if any plumbing or food-contact surfaces are modified). Plan check typically takes 4–12 weeks; if the plans are incomplete or code issues arise, revisions will add time. Once the permit is issued, tenant improvement construction may begin; schedule inspections for rough, final, and certificate of occupancy.
outcomes.note: The catalog confirms stamped architectural plans are needed but does not describe routing to Planning, Section 175, the 4-12 week plan check timeline, or inspection requirements.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the ABC Type 42 license with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, submitting the approved CUA and building permit as supporting documents. What to say: File the ABC Type 42 application online through ABC's licensing portal, including the signed lease, the approved CUA motion, the seller's permit (CDTFA), the business registration certificate (SF Treasurer), the entity registration (CA Secretary of State), and proof that the entity has applied for or received a building permit. Pay the ABC filing fee (approximately $1,000–$1,600 including first-year license fee). ABC will post a public notice at the premises for 30 days and send the application to SF Planning and SFPD for review. Planning will issue a zoning referral approval (routine once the CUA is granted); SFPD will review for location and any concerns. outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain the health permit to operate from SF Department of Public Health after the final building inspection. What to say: Apply online for the health permit through DPH's Environmental Health portal after the building permit final inspection is complete and the space is ready for a pre-opening inspection. The application requires the Business Account Number (SF Treasurer), the Location ID (LIN), and proof that at least one manager or owner has a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate (not required for a bar with no food, but RBS certification for alcohol servers is required under state law). DPH will schedule a pre-opening inspection to confirm that sinks, surfaces, lighting, and waste disposal meet code. The permit is issued after the inspection passes. Do not serve the public before the permit is in hand.
outcomes.note: The cited record is about business registration, not health permits; it contains no information about DPH, health permit procedures, or inspections.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File for the sign permit with SF Planning and DBI if installing or replacing exterior signage. What to say: Submit a sign permit application with drawings of the proposed exterior sign (dimensions, materials, illumination) to Planning for design review and to DBI for structural review. The CCB district may have design guidelines for signage; confirm with Planning whether the sign complies with size and illumination limits (Planning Code Section 602 et seq.). The permit is typically approved in 2–6 weeks if the sign is not in a historic district and does not exceed size limits. Schedule the sign installation after the permit is issued.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $4,155 to $18,250. Notes: The day range (120–300 days) and cost range ($4,155–$18,250 in government fees) are the time and cost to obtain the three approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 per the catalog, depending on construction cost and fee waiver eligibility), Health permit to operate (14–45 days to issue after application, $470 application fee in 2026–27, included in the building permit timeline), and Building permit with change of use (14–120 days for plan check and issuance, $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation, per the catalog). The timeline assumes the CUA is approved at the first hearing and no appeal is filed (add 1–2 months if appealed), that building plans are complete and pass review without major revisions (incomplete plans can add 2–4 months), and that the ABC Type 42 application and PCN finding (if required) proceed in parallel with construction (60–150 days per the catalog, with $1,000–$1,600 in ABC fees not included in this range because the alcohol row status is insufficient information and the ABC license is not in the entitlement path). The cost range includes only the Planning CUA fee, the building permit fee, the health permit application fee, and the SF business registration fee ($55–$700); it does not include architect fees, construction costs, ABC license fees, state business registration ($70–$150), or ongoing costs such as insurance and payroll taxes. If the CUA is denied or the building permit uncovers a code issue that cannot be resolved, the timeline and cost figures do not apply. Confirm the current CUA and building permit fee schedules with Planning and DBI, as fees are adjusted annually for CPI and by construction valuation.
